A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
both endogenous and exogenous spatial attention can induce location transfer, but via different mechanisms.
attentional mechanisms, both exogenous and endogenous, are crucial for perceptual learning, and that the mechanisms of transfer are different for exogenous and endogeneous attention.
covert visual attention, regardless of its type, is a key mechanism for perceptual learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
both types of covert attention, exogenous and endogenous, can be harnessed to overcome the location specificity and improve transfer of perceptual learning.
covert spatial attention can be manipulated during perceptual learning and that this manipulation can induce location transfer.
covert attention, whether it is involuntary or voluntary, can be used to overcome the limitations of perceptual learning.
